cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.title: High-Contrast Card Focus
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.objective: Support visual focus with one bold black-and-white card.
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.description: Baby looks at a single high-contrast card held 8–12 inches away while you describe the pattern.
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.preparation:
Select one simple pattern (stripes or bullseye)
Sit facing baby
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.setup: Baby comfortable on mat; card ready.
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.steps:
1. Hold card steady in view
2. Allow time to focus
3. Move slightly side to side
4. Name pattern simply (stripes/spots)
5. Rest eyes
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.safetyNotes: Sealed laminate edges; no glitter/loose parts.
teacherTips: One card at a time; put extras away.

substitutions.use: large soft household cloth or board book with bold visuals

cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.adaptations: Younger infants: shorter looking time, closer visuals, more face-to-face. Pause at gaze aversion.
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.extensions: If baby stays alert, offer one more brief repetition or a second color/pattern.
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.mixedAgeAdaptations: Birth–3 months: looking/listening focus. 3–6 months: invite reaching/grasping when ready.
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.imageBriefSetup: Caregiver holding one bold B/W stripe card 8–12 inches from infant.
cur-act-80e12e1e8ae7eb21.outdoorAlternatives: If weather and shade allow, offer a brief outdoor version with the same materials.

cur-act-d9160b08b0bdd2e9.title: Tummy Time Pattern Line
cur-act-d9160b08b0bdd2e9.objective: Invite head lifting toward a tummy-time contrast strip.
cur-act-d9160b08b0bdd2e9.description: During supervised tummy time, a printable contrast strip sits at eye level in front of baby.
cur-act-d9160b08b0bdd2e9.materials:
Tummy-time visual strip (printable)
Mat
Optional support roll
Printable (draft): High-Contrast Pattern & Face Cards
cur-act-d9160b08b0bdd2e9.preparation: Place strip along front edge of mat
cur-act-d9160b08b0bdd2e9.setup: Awake tummy time facing the strip.

cur-act-e4d1bb92b67ce15c.title: Bold Card Gaze Garden
cur-act-e4d1bb92b67ce15c.objective: Offer a calm sequence of 2–3 contrast cards for gazing.
cur-act-e4d1bb92b67ce15c.description: You present one card at a time in a quiet ‘garden’ of visuals, watching for focus and break cues.
cur-act-e4d1bb92b67ce15c.materials:
2–3 pattern cards
Mat
Printable (draft): High-Contrast Pattern & Face Cards
cur-act-e4d1bb92b67ce15c.preparation: Order cards from simplest to busier
cur-act-e4d1bb92b67ce15c.setup: Sit with cards face down; show one at a time.
cur-act-e4d1bb92b67ce15c.steps:
1. Show card 1 still
2. Allow gaze
3. Switch to card 2
4. Optional card 3 if still alert
5. Stop at first fatigue cue
cur-act-e4d1bb92b67ce15c.observationOpportunities: Maintains calm alert looking; switches attention.
cur-act-e4d1bb92b67ce15c.safetyNotes: No card stacks within baby’s kick zone as clutter.
teacherTips: Gaze aversion means break, not ‘try harder’.

substitutions.use: large soft household cloth or board book with bold visuals

week.weeklyOverview: High-contrast black-and-white patterns support early visual focus and tracking. The week centers on looking, tummy-time visuals, faces, short books, songs, and caregiver talk — not crafts or worksheets.
week.objectives:
Strengthen visual focus with simple high-contrast patterns
Practice slow tracking of bold cards/objects
Support tummy-time looking with contrast visuals
Use face cards and caregiver faces as primary targets
Offer safe reaching toward large contrast toys when ready

High-contrast pattern cards (printable draft)

week.familyConnection: Share that simple black-and-white cards during alert awake time can support looking — always with your face and voice.
week.adaptations: Younger infants need closer (8–12 in), slower moves, fewer cards. Reduce if overstimulated. Older infants may reach for large contrast toys.

items.title: High-Contrast Card Focus
items.objective: Support visual focus with one bold black-and-white card.
items.description: Baby looks at a single high-contrast card held 8–12 inches away while you describe the pattern.
items.setup: Baby comfortable on mat; card ready.
items.steps:
1. Hold card steady in view
2. Allow time to focus
3. Move slightly side to side
4. Name pattern simply (stripes/spots)
5. Rest eyes
items.teacherRole: One card at a time; put extras away.
items.extensions: If baby stays alert, offer one more brief repetition or a second color/pattern.
items.adaptations: Younger infants: shorter looking time, closer visuals, more face-to-face. Pause at gaze aversion.
items.safetyNotes: Sealed laminate edges; no glitter/loose parts.
items.preparation:
Select one simple pattern (stripes or bullseye)
Sit facing baby

items.title: Bold Card Gaze Garden
items.objective: Offer a calm sequence of 2–3 contrast cards for gazing.
items.description: You present one card at a time in a quiet ‘garden’ of visuals, watching for focus and break cues.
items.materials:
2–3 pattern cards
Mat
Printable (draft): High-Contrast Pattern & Face Cards
items.setup: Sit with cards face down; show one at a time.
items.steps:
1. Show card 1 still
2. Allow gaze
3. Switch to card 2
4. Optional card 3 if still alert
5. Stop at first fatigue cue
items.teacherRole: Gaze aversion means break, not ‘try harder’.
items.observationOpportunities: Maintains calm alert looking; switches attention.
items.extensions: If baby stays alert, offer one more brief repetition or a second color/pattern.
items.adaptations: Younger infants: shorter looking time, closer visuals, more face-to-face. Pause at gaze aversion.
items.safetyNotes: No card stacks within baby’s kick zone as clutter.
items.preparation: Order cards from simplest to busier

items.title: Slow Pattern Arc Track
items.objective: Practice eye tracking along a slow arc with a contrast card.
items.description: Move a patterned card in a slow left–center–right arc while baby watches.
items.materials:
Tracking card (printable)
Mat
Printable (draft): High-Contrast Pattern & Face Cards
items.setup: Baby on back; card in starting left position.
items.steps:
1. Gain attention on card
2. Move slowly left to center
3. Pause
4. Move slowly to right
5. Rest card still
items.teacherRole: If baby loses track, shorten the arc.
items.observationOpportunities: Eyes follow arc; refocuses at pause.
items.extensions: If baby stays alert, offer one more brief repetition or a second color/pattern.

teacherToolkit.teacherPreparation: Present one pattern at a time. Your face remains the richest visual.
teacherToolkit.notes: Printables are draft visuals for attention — not worksheets.
teacherToolkit.familyConnection: Share that simple black-and-white cards during alert awake time can support looking — always with your face and voice.
teacherToolkit.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger infants: closer, slower, shorter bursts. Older infants: offer large graspable items when ready.
teacherToolkit.extraSupportAdaptations: Reduce visuals to one focal item; pause when baby looks away; keep sessions very brief.
teacherToolkit.challengeExtensions: When baby is alert and reaching, widen the tracking arc slightly or offer a second texture.
teacherToolkit.safetyInclusionNotes: Cards laminated with sealed edges or cardstock only; no small parts, strings, or plastic bags. Supervised tummy time; back to sleep.
teacherToolkit.endOfWeekReflection: Which colors/patterns held attention? When did babies disengage? What caregiver language felt natural?
teacherTips: Your face and voice matter more than perfect materials.
Follow the baby’s alert windows — stop early rather than push.
Narrate without expecting verbal answers.
setupCleanupShortcuts: Stage one sensory set at a time
Sanitize mouthed items immediately after use
Return cards/books to a labeled tray
documentationPrompts: Note gaze/tracking moments in plain language for families
Photo of setup (not staged ‘perfect’ baby performance)
